GCPercent.note: FastQC on the raw reads; single-end runs write it on the sample row, paired-end on <sample>_1 (@R1). 2.0.0's MultiQC 1.35 spells it fastqc-, 1.0.4's MultiQC 1.18 FastQC_mqc-generalstats-fastqc-; the trimmed reads' FastQC (<sample>_1_val_1) is never folded

F_bp.note: mean read-1 length (FastQC per-read row, else the single-end sample row)

NumAligned.note: STAR's exact uniquely mapped reads from <aligner>/log/<sample>.Log.final.out; else MultiQC 1.18's column, which is the raw count (MultiQC 1.35's star-uniquely_mapped is in millions and is ruled out)

MismatchPercent.note: a percentage in 2.0.0's MultiQC 1.35; MultiQC 1.18 (1.0.4) writes a 0-1 fraction, which $derived.mismatch_pct turns into a percentage

AssignedPercent.note: 2.0.0 writes featureCounts on the <sample>_sorted row (the BAM's name), which qc_row_suffixes folds onto the sample

deliberately_unmapped.why: Sequence-level duplication before alignment; DuplicationPercent is alignment-based (Picard), and mixing the two definitions in one field would mislead.
Same as the average length; hidden when samples agree within 10 bp.
Share of FastQC modules that failed: a report summary, not a measurement.
Count in millions; NumReads/TotalReads hold read counts.
MultiQC 1.35 prints it in millions; NumAligned and MappedPercent already record the alignment.
STAR's uniquely mapped plus multimapped reads, in millions (MultiQC adds the two). NumAligned holds the exact uniquely mapped count from the STAR log.
STAR's uniquely mapped plus multimapped percent (MultiQC adds the two); MappedPercent records the uniquely mapped share, as in 1.0.4.
MultiQC 1.35 prints it in millions. NumAligned reads the exact count from the STAR log ($derived.uniquely_mapped_reads).
